coverageLimitation: This engine evaluates what the providers below publish. There is no global cell-by-cell scan, and no claim is made about hazards outside each provider’s stated reach. A place absent from every provider was not examined and must not be read as quiet.

gdacs.label: GDACS (Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System)
gdacs.coverageResolution: Only events GDACS itself raises to an alert level. Flood, drought and wildfire records describe alert areas, not incident points.
gdacs.completenessBasis: GDACS lists only events it raises to an alert level, so a disaster it does not carry may simply be below that threshold.
gdacs.inputBasis: GDACS raises alerts on events it has already detected, so its records say what is happening rather than what will.

usgs.label: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program
usgs.coverageResolution: Every earthquake of magnitude 2.5 or above in the past seven days, at its epicentre. Anything smaller, or older, is outside this feed.
usgs.completenessBasis: A complete catalogue of earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 and above for the past seven days, so an absence above that threshold is meaningful.
usgs.inputBasis: A catalogue of earthquakes that have occurred.

emsc.label: EMSC (European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre)
emsc.geographicCoverage: Global, with the densest network in Europe and the Mediterranean
emsc.coverageResolution: Earthquakes of magnitude 4.5 or above, at epicentre.
emsc.inputBasis: A catalogue of earthquakes that have occurred.

eonet.label: NASA EONET
eonet.coverageResolution: A curated set of events drawn from Earth-observation sources. EONET does not claim to list every event, so absence here is not evidence of absence.
eonet.completenessBasis: A curated set; EONET does not claim to list every event, so its silence is not evidence.
eonet.inputBasis: A curated catalogue of natural events already under way.

nhc.label: NOAA National Hurricane Center
nhc.geographicCoverage: Atlantic, eastern Pacific and central Pacific basins only
nhc.coverageResolution: Active tropical cyclones, at storm centre. Storms in the western Pacific, Indian Ocean and southern hemisphere are outside this provider entirely.
nhc.completenessBasis: Every active tropical cyclone in the basins it publishes for.
nhc.inputBasis: The hurricane centre publishes advisories for active systems, including where a storm is expected to go, which is an input to a forecast of what it has not yet done.

nws.label: NOAA / National Weather Service
nws.geographicCoverage: United States and its territories only
nws.coverageResolution: Alerts at severe or extreme severity, carrying the affected-area polygon where the agency published one and a forecast-zone centre where it did not.
nws.completenessBasis: Exhaustive for active warnings, but a warning is not an observation: these records never enter the observed-disaster ledger, so this provider cannot establish that no disaster occurred.
nws.inputBasis: A watch or warning states that severe weather is expected, which is a statement about what has not happened yet.

reliefweb.label: ReliefWeb (UN OCHA)
reliefweb.coverageResolution: Country-level humanitarian disaster declarations. These carry no incident coordinates and are placed at a country centroid.
reliefweb.completenessBasis: Only disasters ReliefWeb has declared, which is a subset of those that occur.
reliefweb.inputBasis: Situation reports and declarations published after a disaster has occurred.

usgs_volcano.label: USGS Volcano Hazards Program
usgs_volcano.geographicCoverage: Volcanoes monitored by the United States volcano observatories
usgs_volcano.coverageResolution: Volcanoes currently at an elevated alert level. Volcanoes outside the US observatory network are not covered by this provider.
usgs_volcano.completenessBasis: Exhaustive for elevated alert levels in the observatory network it covers, which is not the same as exhaustive for eruptions that caused harm: an alert level is a published status, these records never enter the observed-disaster ledger, and their silence establishes only that nothing was elevated.
usgs_volcano.inputBasis: A volcano alert level states expected activity - a watch or warning is issued for unrest before an eruption, not after it.

providerVersionNote: Each scan records the provider definitions in force when it ran, under providerVersions. A definition is never applied backwards: widening a provider’s scope or calling it exhaustive changes what future scans can establish, never what past ones did.

retention.note: Per-scan detail is held for the most recent 2000 scans. Coverage before detailFrom cannot be established from this ledger and must be reported as DATA_UNAVAILABLE, never as scanned or unscanned.
